messages:
Sofia: Incoming escalation from BetaLabs — rerank API returning weird values or 400s after copying cURL from Console. They say behavior differs between bash and PowerShell.

Customer: "We copied the cURL snippet from the Console and sometimes get a 400, sometimes we get all scores ~0.0000 and every candidate equal. Were on hosted. Pulled the sample into PowerShell. Example below, exact paste.

```powershell
# paste from Console into PowerShell
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank `\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $env:API_KEY\" `\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" `\n  -d '{\"query\": \"how to reset\", \"candidates\": '[\"Email reset\",\"Admin reset\"]'}'
```

Customer: "This either 400s or returns: {\"results\": [{\"id\":\"Email reset\",\"score\":0.000000},{\"id\":\"Admin reset\",\"score\":0.000000}]} which is wrong (should prefer Email reset)."

Sofia: Thanks. Two likely causes: Console snippet uses single quotes around -d and inner content includes double quotes / arrays; in PowerShell the quoting rules differ and our copy path is producing malformed JSON (candidates becomes a string). Also some customers had previously seen probability-like examples in docs and applied softmax client-side. If you softmax logits twice or on already-normalized numbers you can get near-uniform tiny floats.

support-bot: automated: Error observed from client: 400 InvalidCandidateFormat. Details: candidates must be an array of strings or objects. Request body parsed as {\"candidates\": \"[... ]\"}. Logged incident reference: INC-8942.

Dan: Can BetaLabs paste the exact response body and headers? Also, are they sending candidate objects or strings?

Customer: Pasted response headers and body: 

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json

{ "results": [ { "id": "Email reset", "score": 2.7 }, { "id": "Admin reset", "score": 2.7 } ] }
```

Customer: "We got 200 with identical logits sometimes and a 400 other times. Were on PowerShell on Windows 11."

Dan: Identical logits is suspicious but explained if the client is post-processing incorrectly. Example: if BetaLabs took our example that showed normalized numbers and applied softmax themselves, then later applied softmax again, they could compress differences. Also JSON parsing differences in PowerShell can turn arrays into strings.

Priya: I dug into docs. There was an older example that showed probability-like numbers in the results section; the current API returns raw model scores (logits). Docs wording is ambiguous in one paragraph. Ill patch that. Also Console's \"Copy cURL\" emits a single-quoted blob which is safe for POSIX shells but not PowerShell. We need platform-specific snippets.

Dan: Quick repro I ran locally on mac and on Windows:

Bad (PowerShell paste from Console):
```powershell
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank `\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $env:API_KEY\" `\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" `\n  -d '{\"query\":\"how to reset\",\"candidates\":\"[\\\"Email reset\\\",\\\"Admin reset\\\"]\"}'
```

Good (PowerShell-safe using double quotes and escape backticks):
```powershell
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $env:API_KEY\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  --data-binary \"{\\\"query\\\":\\\"how to reset\\\",\\\"candidates\\\":[\\\"Email reset\\\",\\\"Admin reset\\\"]}\"
```

Good (bash/zsh):
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' \\\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n  --data-binary '{"query":"how to reset","candidates":["Email reset","Admin reset"]}'
```

Dan: Note the difference: --data-binary avoids the shell trying to interpret the JSON. In PowerShell you must use double-quoted payloads with escaped inner quotes. Console should offer a platform toggle.

Priya: Action items for docs/console:
- Docs: clarify \"scores are raw logits (higher is better); normalize client-side if you need probabilities\" and remove any stray probability-only examples.
- Console: add a copy toggle for Bash / PowerShell / Windows CMD and emit platform-appropriate quoting.
- Console: add a small help tooltip near Rerank that says \"Scores are raw model outputs (logits).\"

Dan: Runtime action items: add clearer 400 payload error messages (machine-readable code, e.g., {\"error_code\":\"invalid_candidates\",\"expected\":\"array\",\"received\":\"string\"}) and a 413 explicit candidate_count_exceeded with limit=512. I'll open RUN-412. Also consider a non-breaking query param normalize=true to return probabilities (opt-in) — need perf estimate.

Sofia: I sent BetaLabs a minimal PowerShell example (the one above with --data-binary) and a small JS softmax snippet to convert logits to probabilities if they want: 

```js
// convert logits to probabilities
function softmax(logits) {\n  const max = Math.max(...logits);\n  const exps = logits.map(x => Math.exp(x - max));\n  const sum = exps.reduce((a,b) => a + b, 0);\n  return exps.map(e => e / sum);\n}
```

Sofia: BetaLabs tried the PowerShell-safe payload and confirmed ranking is correct now. They asked for a console notice about logits vs probs to avoid PM confusion.

Priya: I opened DOCS-589 to update the page and CON-207 to implement platform-specific cURL snippets in Console. Dan opened RUN-412 for runtime error clarity and optional normalization.

Sofia: Marking this escalation as resolved pending PR merges and Console change. BetaLabs satisfied with workaround. Tagging @Priya to land docs update and @Dan to track runtime ticket. :rocket:

support-bot: automated: Escalation resolved by Sofia at 1792345900.
